title: All Passengers Saved: The Night a Private Wire Outran Every Official Channel and Printed a Lie
participants: press associations of the North Atlantic ports

extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: Wireless telegraphy was a private commercial service — Marconi Company operators aboard ships, paid by message and by contract, whose bulletins were the product sold to a hungry press within hours of the disaster.
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: No government or company channel existed to verify or suppress wireless traffic; the Marconi operators' relayed dispatches moved directly from the ether to front pages, and the press associations ran them without source discipline.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: The first bulletins — Titanic safe, in tow, all passengers saved, Halifax the destination of the towed liner — ran the morning of April 16 in Halifax and across the North Atlantic press; the garbled relay chain and the operators' commercial incentives structured the fog.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: The wireless companies' monopoly on fast news was the windfall: speed sold papers and messages, and the error was corrected only when slower official channels caught up — when the Carpathia docked in New York on April 18 and the first accurate lists replaced the fiction.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: The fog closed as a story of technology's teething pains rather than a structural account of a private information infrastructure printing unverified disaster news; the falsified casualty reports were left to folklore, not to any accounting.

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: The fog inherited the Marconi Company's monopoly on ship-to-shore traffic and the press associations' competitive wire economy, both built on speed as the salable product.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: The April 1912 fog established the standard crisis-information pattern of the twentieth century: private infrastructure first, official confirmation last, with the gap between filled by whoever owns the fastest channel.
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: The error cost the press nothing that mattered to the wire companies: the same channels that printed the false safety of the morning sold the corrected horror of the evening, and speed — not accuracy — remained the priced good.
closedLoopRatchet.enablesNextDossier: The pattern of private-speed, official-silence information gaps became the standard fog of every later market crash and disaster in this atlas, priced and sold by whoever owned the wire.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: The romantic image of the wireless operators as heroes whose brave Morse saved hundreds — the story of Jack Phillips and Harold Bride holding the key to the end.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: The hero story erases the opposite ledger: the same commercial wire that transmitted the distress calls also transmitted the false dispatches that Halifax printed as truth, and its owners sold speed with no verification duty at all.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: The documented record: April 15-16 bulletins reporting the Titanic safe and in tow, Halifax papers running the false report the morning of April 16, and the correction arriving only with the Carpathia's April 18 landing — preserved in the Library of Congress's contemporary press record.
